metadata.schedule_summary: Day 1: bevacizumab and folinic acid, then fluorouracil bolus and a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. Repeat every 14 days while treatment is helping and remains tolerable. This regimen does not include oxaliplatin or irinotecan.
metadata.licensing_note: NCCP 00791 v 2 pp 8–9: unlicensed bevacizumab regimen in Ireland; patient information/consent and local Drugs and Therapeutics governance required. Rapid infusion is separately unlicensed.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or other appropriately authorised specialist named in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Use the most restrictive applicable component rule and confirm dose changes against the current official NCCP PDF.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: JSON assessment encoding derived from NCCP 00791 version 2. Confirm the current official NCCP PDF and use independent clinical judgement. Independent clinical and oncology-pharmacy validation remain pending.

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No other non-haematological adverse event.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Grade 1 under the named CTCAE term: generally mild or asymptomatic, with observation only and no intervention indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Grade 2 under the named CTCAE term: generally moderate; local/non-invasive intervention may be indicated and instrumental activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Grade 3 under the named CTCAE term: severe or medically significant; hospital care may be indicated and self-care activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Grade 4 under the named CTCAE term: life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

other_nonhaem_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the exact adverse event and use its toxicity-specific CTCAE definition; assess symptoms, intervention and functional impact before selecting the grade.

diarrhoea_grade.label: Current diarrhoea grade (confirm against NCCP Table 6)

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No diarrhoea above usual baseline.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Increase of 2–3 stools/day or mild increase in loose watery colostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools, nocturnal stools or mild increase in loose watery colostomy output.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Increase of 7–9 stools/day, incontinence, malabsorption or severe increase in loose watery colostomy output.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Increase of 10 or more stools/day, grossly bloody colostomy output, or loose watery output requiring parenteral support; dehydration.

diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade using increase in stools over baseline, ostomy output, need for hospitalisation and impact on self-care; do not grade from the word “diarrhoea” alone. NCCP 00791 Table 6 prints older symptom-based grades that are not identical to CTCAE 5.0. Confirm the source-table grade before selecting a dose-level change; a CTCAE grade alone must not silently substitute for the source criteria. proteinuria_grade.label: Proteinuria grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No proteinuria.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Dipstick 1+ or protein below 1.0 g per 24 hours.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Dipstick 2+ or 3+, or protein 1.0 to under 3.5 g per 24 hours.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Protein 3.5 g or more per 24 hours or dipstick 4+; quantify according to the protocol.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Grade 4 is not defined under the CTCAE proteinuria term; use the appropriate renal-disorder term for life-threatening renal consequences.

proteinuria_grade.assessment_guidance: Use urine protein quantification and clinical consequences; dipstick alone may require confirmatory UPCR or 24-hour urine assessment.

diarrhoea_highest_grade.label: Highest diarrhoea grade
diarrhoea_highest_grade.assessment_guidance: Count stools per day above the patient's baseline, assess ostomy output, continence, hydration, fever, abdominal pain, haemodynamic compromise and whether hospital care is indicated. NCCP 00791 Table 6 prints older symptom-based grades that are not identical to CTCAE 5.0. Confirm the source-table grade before selecting a dose-level change; a CTCAE grade alone must not silently substitute for the source criteria.

source_toxicity_grade_confirmed.label: Current and highest GI-toxicity grades reconciled to NCCP Table 6
source_toxicity_grade_confirmed.help_text: NCCP Table 6 diarrhoea: grade 3 7–9 extra stools/day/incontinence/malabsorption or severe watery colostomy output; grade 4 ≥10, gross blood or parenteral support/dehydration. Stomatitis grade 3 unable to eat; grade 4 mucosal necrosis/enteral support/dehydration. Clinical assessment is required where modern CTCAE differs.

uncontrolled_or_symptomatic_hypertension.label: Uncontrolled or symptomatic hypertension on day 1

bp_sustained_on_antihypertensives.label: BP elevation is sustained while taking antihypertensive medication

hypertension_grade.label: Clinically assessed hypertension grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No hypertension.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Systolic 120–139 or diastolic 80–89 mmHg; follow CTCAE adult criteria.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Systolic 140–159 or diastolic 90–99 mmHg; intervention/medication change indicated; assess persistence and symptoms.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Systolic≥160 or diastolic≥100 mmHg; medical intervention and more than one drug or more intensive therapy indicated.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, e.g. malignant hypertension, neurological deficit or hypertensive crisis; urgent intervention indicated.

hypertension_grade.assessment_guidance: Use repeated blood pressure readings, symptoms and medication history. NCCP Table 5 separately defines uncontrolled initiation BP as sustained >150/100 mmHg despite antihypertensive treatment; enter that clinical judgement separately. Grade 4 or persistent grade 3 requires discontinuation.

te_or_grade4_fistula.label: Tracheoesophageal fistula or any grade 4 fistula

haemorrhage_grade.label: Haemorrhage grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No bleeding.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild; intervention not indicated, using the site-specific CTCAE haemorrhage definition.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate; medical intervention indicated; apply the site-specific haemorrhage definition.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe; transfusion, invasive intervention or hospital care indicated as defined for the bleeding site.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated.

haemorrhage_grade.assessment_guidance: Use the site-specific haemorrhage term and document intervention, transfusion, admission and haemodynamic effects. NCCP Table 5 stops bevacizumab for grade 3 or worse bleeding.

action.recommendation: Hold treatment for ANC <1.0; check FBC weekly up to 2 times. Restart only after recovery ≥1 within 2 weeks and review the lowest delayed-week ANC. Reassess the overall combination.

action.recommendation: ANC remains <1.0 after 2 weeks: discontinue the fluorouracil-based treatment pathway. Review the overall regimen; this does not independently assert permanent bevacizumab discontinuation.

action.recommendation: After both counts recover within 2 weeks, reduce both fluorouracil components by 1 dose level for delayed-week ANC <1 (including <0.5). Apply the greatest reduction per component, not the sum of overlapping triggers. Folinic acid remains 400 mg/m² at levels 0/−1/−2; delay/omit it with the 5-FU bolus. Below level−2 means discontinue.

action.recommendation: 24-hour urine protein >4 g: discontinue bevacizumab. No bevacizumab dose reduction is recommended.

rules.explanation: 24-hour urine protein >4 g: discontinue bevacizumab. No bevacizumab dose reduction is recommended.

action.recommendation: Protein >2 to 4 g/24 hours: hold bevacizumab; repeat 24-hour urine every 2 weeks and resume only when ≤2 g/24 hours.

action.recommendation: Urine protein ≤2 g/24 hours meets this source proteinuria criterion. Other entered restrictions govern; this result alone does not establish eligibility or override grade 4 proteinuria.

action.recommendation: Dipstick 2+/3+ or laboratory urine protein ≥1 g/L: Table 4 permits the scheduled bevacizumab dose from this domain, with 24-hour collection within 3 days before the next dose. A concurrent 4+ or 24-hour hold/stop result takes priority; concentration g/L is not g/24 hours.

action.recommendation: Source initiating-treatment definition is sustained BP >150/100 mmHg while taking antihypertensives. A single reading or isolated threshold must not silently substitute for persistence/treatment context; assess symptoms and clinical control.

eligibility: Indication as listed in the current official NCCP regimen
Performance status and organ function appropriate for the selected treatment
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
monitoring: Baseline FBC, renal/liver profile, urine protein dipstick, BP and cardiac history/examination; DPD before first fluorouracil unless previously tested.
ECG as clinically indicated; consider ECHO with prior anthracycline treatment or chest-wall radiation.
Each cycle: FBC, renal/liver profile, urine protein dipstick. BP before each cycle AND after treatment.
On warfarin: INR weekly until dose stable, then before each cycle. Disease imaging and additional testing follow the individual treatment plan.
dose_modifications: See executable source-specific rules: fluorouracil dose levels and recovery windows are separate from bevacizumab hold/stop rules.
Bevacizumab dose reduction for adverse events is not recommended.
Mild/moderate hepatic impairment without renal impairment needs no expected fluorouracil adjustment; severe hepatic impairment is not recommended. No imported bilirubin 85/AST 180 rule.
